title: Repo restructure: npm workspaces, TypeScript strict scaffold, root scripts, Vercel project skeleton
objective: Restructure the repository into the target Vercel-deployable monorepo layout (spec section 8): npm workspaces root, api/ Vercel function entrypoint directory, src/server backend tree, scripts/ tree, docs stubs, and strict TypeScript + Vitest tooling for the backend, without touching the existing .NET tree (which remains the behavioral reference until T-044).
scope: Root package.json with npm workspaces (root + src/ui + e2e_tests) on Node 22 LTS and the M-19 script names stubbed (dev, dev:vercel, supabase:start|stop|reset, db:migrate, db:seed, db:types, typecheck, lint, test, test:integration, cron:list, cron:run, cron:run:all, queue:worker, queue:enqueue:test, jobs:status) — stubs may exit with a not-yet-implemented message where the target does not exist yet

Directory scaffold: api/ (v1/, cron/, queue/), src/server/{lib/{config,db,auth,tenancy,validation,errors,logging,storage,supabase,router},domains,jobs/{cron,queue},tests}, scripts/{jobs,db}, docs/ stubs (local-development.md, deployment.md, background-jobs.md, environment-variables.md as placeholders)
TypeScript strict-mode tsconfig for the backend (no any, server code excluded from client bundles); shared base config if useful
vercel.json skeleton: Vite framework preset compatibility, functions config placeholder (runtime/maxDuration), explicitly NO cron registrations (scheduling is pg_cron in migrations)
.gitignore updates (.env*, .vercel, logs, transient artifacts); .env.example and .env.local.example skeletons with placeholder entries only
Vitest configuration for backend unit and integration test projects under src/server/tests
ESLint (or the existing lint tooling) wired for the new backend tree
out_of_scope: Any migration, seed, or runtime code
Deleting or modifying the .NET tree, docker-compose, or e2e suite
implementation_details: Root package.json: "workspaces": ["src/ui", "e2e_tests"], engines.node >=22, private true. Dependencies added at root for the backend per approved set only: zod, kysely, pg, hono, @supabase/supabase-js, exceljs (may defer to consuming tasks), devDependencies: typescript, tsx, vitest, @types/pg, @types/node.

api/ entrypoint files are created as placeholders only where needed to validate the Vercel layout (real Hono app lands in T-009); do not create one function per route — the target is api/v1/[[...segments]].ts catch-all plus dedicated api/cron/* and api/queue/drain.ts.
tsconfig: strict true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess recommended, module/target suitable for Node 22 Vercel functions; separate tsconfig for src/ui remains untouched.
vercel.json: keep minimal — no crons key ever; document in a comment-adjacent README note that schedules live in supabase/migrations pg_cron entries (M-22).
npm scripts that cannot run yet must fail loudly with a clear message rather than silently succeed, so CI wiring in T-010 stays honest.
Existing src/ui and e2e_tests packages must still install and build unchanged (npm install from clean checkout, npm run build -w src/ui).

unit: No pure-logic units introduced; placeholder Vitest smoke test proving the backend test project runs (vitest executes and passes from root script)
integration: npm install from clean checkout succeeds on Node 22
npm run typecheck passes for the scaffold; npm run build -w src/ui still builds the SPA unchanged
Stubbed scripts exit non-zero with a clear not-implemented message
e2e: None at this stage (existing Playwright suite untouched and still points at the .NET stack)

findings.summary: AC-001/V-001 clause `npm run build -w src/ui` exits 0 cannot be met: the SPA build is already red with 18 pre-existing TypeScript errors, independent of this task.
findings.detail: `npm run build -w src/ui` (tsc -b && vite build) fails with exit 2 and 18 TS errors in src/ui sources (recharts 3.9.2 typings, @types/react 18.3.31 LegacyRef, noUncheckedIndexedAccess violations, SortableTh generic misuse, a broken test file). Proven pre-existing: src/ui was copied to a temp directory outside the workspace and installed with `npm ci` from its own committed src/ui/package-lock.json (identical versions: recharts 3.9.2, @types/react 18.3.31, typescript 6.0.3, react 18.3.1); the isolated build fails with a byte-identical error-location set (md5 14890d8de9e62539ef23727bee74abdd, 18 errors) to the workspace build. Bundling alone is fine: `npx vite build` in the isolated copy exits 0 - only the tsc type gate fails. The failure was previously masked by a stale src/ui/node_modules/.tmp tsbuildinfo, which `tsc -b` used to skip the type pass; a fresh install removes it. T-001 is forbidden to edit src/ui sources, so this needs an explicit decision: (a) a scoped SPA type-error fix task before AC-001 can pass, or (b) amend AC-001/V-001 to require `npx vite build` (bundle) plus a separately tracked SPA typecheck debt item.
findings.resolution: Resolved via T-045 (human chose option (a): fix the SPA type errors; AC-001/V-001 unchanged). Evaluator independently verified 2026-07-18: `rm -rf src/ui/node_modules/.tmp` then `npm run build -w src/ui` EXIT 0 with both tsbuildinfo files regenerated during the run, proving the tsc type pass executed from a clean (uncached) state.

findings.summary: src/ui/package-lock.json is now redundant under npm workspaces and can drift from the root lockfile.
findings.detail: The root package-lock.json is authoritative for all workspaces; the nested src/ui/package-lock.json is ignored by npm during workspace installs but was still used to prove F-001-1 pre-existence. Left in place because T-001 must not modify src/ui; recommend removing it in the task that next touches the SPA.

findings.summary: lint-no-any.test.ts writes a fixed-name fixture (src/server/lib/errors/lint-any-fixture.tmp.ts) into the production tree, making the test suite unsafe to run concurrently with itself.
findings.detail: The test writes the temp any-fixture into src/server/lib/errors/ and runs npm run lint (repo-wide). A second concurrent vitest invocation (observed during T-003/T-007 parallel execution) sees the fixture via its own lint/scan runs and fails transiently. Within one vitest run this is safe (integration project has fileParallelism:false and unit tests do not lint), but two simultaneous npm test invocations race. config-env-access.test.ts (T-007) also runs npm run lint and is a collision victim, not a cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) name the fixture uniquely per run (e.g. lint-any-fixture.<pid>.tmp.ts) and lint only that file via eslint --stdin --stdin-filename instead of a repo-wide lint, or (b) T-010 CI must guarantee vitest invocations never run in parallel. Remediation delegated to T-010; T-001 status unchanged (recorded by evaluator during T-003/T-007 review at orchestrator direction).
findings.resolution: Fixed by T-010. Root cause confirmed: ESLint does not honour .gitignore, so `eslint .` linted the transient lint-any-fixture whenever a concurrent vitest run had it on disk. Fix: '**/*.tmp.ts' added to eslint config `ignores` so a repo-wide lint can never observe a transient fixture, PLUS a per-run unique fixture name (${pid}-${Date.now()}) so two concurrent copies cannot delete each other's file. The lint gate is NOT weakened - the failing case now lints its fixture by explicit path with --no-ignore (new lint:path script), still evaluating the real root config. Evidence with the fixture on disk: repo-wide lint exit 0; explicit-path lint exit 1 citing @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any. A third test permanently encodes the invariant ('keeps a repo-wide lint green while a transient fixture is on disk').
